clue.text: Aquatic plant foreign to the Isle of Man?

definitions.meaning: a reedmace or bulrush growing in water, named for its furry brown spike

definitions.text: foreign to the Isle of Man?
definitions.meaning: the Manx cat of the Isle of Man is famously born without this appendage

explanation.surface: A question about whether a water plant grows on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, is home to the Manx cat, which has no tail; so the feline's appendage is unknown there.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedmace is commonly called by this name for its long furry flower spike.

clue.text: I travel the Province with a female artist

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
to go is to travel
NI, Northern Ireland, is known as the Province

explanation.surface: Someone touring Northern Ireland with a woman companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Province' is a common name for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietro Annigoni was an Italian painter famous for his portraits of Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Son's audible faux pas about conveniently placed drink

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
handy means near at hand

indicators.note: the faux pas word is heard rather than seen, so its sound-alike is taken

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: A son's blunder, made in earshot, about a drink sitting within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link: concerning. GAFF sounds like GAFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandygaff is an old name for beer mixed with ginger beer or lemonade.

clue.text: Rear parts of hospital viewed later?

parts.note: after is the nautical word for at the rear, as in the after deck
wards are rooms in a hospital

explanation.surface: A question about the back wards of a hospital being inspected later.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards and later are synonyms for at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Sealant placed round clear opening in dome

indicators.note: the sealant word surrounds the clear word

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints
net means clear after deductions, as in net profit

explanation.surface: Sealing compound applied around a transparent hole in a cupola.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a crescent or round window or opening in a dome or vault.

clue.text: Anxious youth leader holding up centre of barrier

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below and supports the first
the barrier word loses its outer letters, leaving its middle

parts.note: a hedge is a barrier of shrubs

indicators.note: the leader of youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nervous youth leader is delaying the middle of the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy is a colloquial synonym for nervous or anxious.

clue.text: Mess up finally, seeing nothing odd in secret observation

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are discarded, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone finally makes a mess of an undercover surveillance job, noticing nothing unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is the act of spying, watching secretly.

clue.text: Capital letter, some say, for Bounty

indicators.note: the phrase is taken as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: a capital S is a large S

explanation.surface: The capital letter of the word Bounty, as some pronounce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity in giving, a bounty.

clue.text: Submarine requiring no end of protective coating

indicators.note: the final letter of the coating word is dropped, so its end is lost

parts.note: underseal is a protective layer sprayed on a car's underside

explanation.surface: A submarine needs a protective coating to keep it watertight.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, submarine means situated beneath the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Popular move, keeping this initially unimpaired

indicators.note: the popular-move pair holds the next letter inside it, as if keeping it safe

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an act is a deed or move

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word this is taken

explanation.surface: A crowd-pleasing manoeuvre that leaves everything undamaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left whole and undamaged is unimpaired; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Just what's needed, these leaders having left the lot!

indicators.note: the leading letters of the word these, T and H, depart from the phrase

parts.note: the very thing is an idiom for exactly what is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone finds exactly what they want, then the bosses walk off with all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these leaders' names the first two letters of 'these'; they leave THE VERY THING.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase the lot is colloquial for all of something, the whole amount.

clue.text: Angular lad concealing name

indicators.note: the lad word hides the next piece inside it

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A thin, sharp-featured young man hiding his identity.
explanation.definitionFit: A bony face or figure is thin with prominent angles, so angular.

clue.text: Up north, forces 23 to be reorganised

indicators.note: the letters of the 23-across answer are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 23 across, the jazz pianist's name

explanation.surface: Military forces in the north are to be restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is a northern English (Cumbrian, Yorkshire) dialect word for a waterfall, from Old Norse; 'Up north' flags the regional usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a force is a cascade of water, so forces are falls.

clue.text: Pay level always accepted, including rise for miners

indicators.note: the level word takes the rest inside it

parts.note: a rate is a level, as in rate of pay

indicators.note: the always word has the miners piece inside it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

indicators.note: in a down clue the miners word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the NUM was Britain's National Union of Mineworkers

explanation.surface: A pay level is always accepted, with a raise for miners.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers; E'ER is the poetic contraction of 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: To remunerate is to pay someone for work or services.

clue.text: Gem a queen originally acquired, found in the sea

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word acquired is taken

parts.note: marine means of or found in the sea

explanation.surface: A jewel a queen first obtained was discovered under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquamarine is a blue-green beryl used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Freakish current unknown in sandbank, note

indicators.note: the current and unknown pieces are put inside the sandbank word

parts.note: a bar is a ridge of sand across a river mouth
I is the symbol for electric current
Z is a mathematical unknown
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A strange current flows over a sandbank, worth a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre and freakish are synonyms, both meaning strikingly odd.

clue.text: Promote cashier, giving rise to explosion

parts.note: to back is to support or promote
as a verb, to cashier is to dismiss, to fire

explanation.surface: Promoting a bank teller leads to an outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' here is the verb meaning dismiss, not the bank teller it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A backfire is an explosion in an engine's exhaust or intake.

clue.text: Urge, way back, to introduce edible seeds

indicators.note: the first piece comes before and leads in the second
the way word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, a way
pulses are peas, beans and lentils

explanation.surface: A desire, going back, to bring lentils into the diet.
explanation.walkthrough: MI here is the M1, Britain's London-to-Leeds motorway, a standard crossword 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge or desire to act.

clue.text: Music used for relaxation around acting area

indicators.note: the relaxation phrase goes round the acting word

parts.note: an armchair is sat in, used for relaxation
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: Soothing music played around the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used for relaxation' reads as SAT IN, as an armchair is; ON sits inside it, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonatina is a short, simple sonata, a piece of music.

clue.text: Summit introducing Sir Rowland to power?

parts.note: Sir Rowland Hill reformed the British postal system
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A summit meeting bringing a Victorian postal reformer to power.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Rowland Hill introduced the Penny Post in Britain in 1840.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilltop is the summit of a hill.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of sins once out of order

indicators.note: the letters are jumbled rather than in their proper sequence

explanation.surface: Admitting to sins that were once committed out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: A confession is an admission, an acknowledgement of guilt or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Recording husband pinched from unimportant person

indicators.note: the husband letter is stolen out of the person word

parts.note: a nothing is a nobody, an insignificant person

explanation.surface: A husband was robbed by a nobody while making a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means writing down or recording.

clue.text: This can be made up, remember

definitions.meaning: you make up your thinking faculty when you reach a decision
as a verb, to take care or bear in ...

explanation.definitionFit: To mind can mean to remember or heed, and one makes up one's mind.

clue.text: Jazzman, unlike Jack Sprat, kicking out old wife

indicators.note: the old and wife pieces are expelled from the phrase

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat, so his opposite gulps it down

explanation.surface: A jazz musician, no lean eater, gets rid of his former spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat, of the English nursery rhyme, 'could eat no fat'; one unlike him swallows fat. 'kicking out' removes OW.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas 'Fats' Waller was a celebrated American jazz pianist and composer.

clue.text: Tip given in article: exercise vote

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
PE is physical education, exercise
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A piece of advice handed out in a newspaper piece on a gym ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the tip or highest point of something.

clue.text: Girl from Channel Islands among others?

indicators.note: the islands abbreviation goes inside the others word

parts.note: alia is Latin for other things, as in inter alia

explanation.surface: A young woman from Jersey or Guernsey mingling with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicia is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Mexican farmer managed business with woman's involvement

parts.note: ran means managed

indicators.note: the woman's piece is wrapped up inside the business word

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A Mexican farmer ran a firm with his wife taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchero is a Mexican rancher or farmer.

clue.text: Lacking refinement, live in Alpine resort

indicators.note: the live word is placed within the rearranged letters
re-sort, sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Being unsophisticated while living in a ski town.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian means common or vulgar, so lacking polish and refinement.
